facts.name: George L. Singeltary II
facts.assignment: Citrus circuit judge. Profile gives general hearing and order procedures but no complete division allocation; county assignment reconciliation pending.

procedure_address_lines: Attn: Circuit Judge George L. Singeltary II
contact.contact_note: Orders inbox is distinct from assistant contact. Suite1-331 is office location; #101 is the specific mailed-evidence address in procedure text. Shared office/assistant phone; not a personal judge contact.

chambers_communications.summary: Email assistant, copying all parties/counsel on all correspondence including scheduling and proposed orders. No direct merits communications or legal advice from assistant.

hearing_scheduling.summary: Email assistant rather than telephone with case/county, motion and total time; coordinate offered dates with all parties, confirm selection and supply courtesy hearing notice. Notice includes motion filing/docket information and courtroom/Zoom details. Unresolved scheduling disagreement goes to court by motion documenting attempts.

proposed_orders.summary: Email only to dedicated orders inbox, .docx without e-Portal formatting codes; PDFs only for attachments. Include motion, cover letter identifying hearing/agreement and certificate of service. For self-represented parties outside electronic service, include the stated mailed-service and filed-certification provision. Do not substitute the shared portal template requirement.

courtesy_copies.summary: Send hearing/cancellation notices to office. In-person evidence: hard copies ready at hearing. Virtual evidence uses clerk premarking and mailed delivery ten business days ahead; over50pages fifteen days to stated #101 address. Profile provides alternative self-marking/indexing if clerk appointment unavailable; detailed evidence merits not analyzed.

remote_appearances.summary: Request Zoom link from assistant with party/case, reason and date; include supplied access information in notice. A request is not independently treated as permission.

cancellations.summary: Notify assistant with reason; file cancellation if hearing notice filed, notify parties and send courtesy copy. Continuance requires filed motion and hearing or party consent, remains subject to court approval; coordinate new date through assistant.

facts.summary: Email-based coordinated scheduling and separate Word-order inbox. Judge expressly rejects portal codes, unlike shared circuit guide. Keep office and evidence-mailing addresses distinct.

review_scope.collected: Complete profile HTML and text; shared order-guide original already retained in Lambert checkpoint.
review_scope.content_reviewed: Contacts, ordinary hearing/Zoom scheduling, cancellation, evidence delivery, proposed-order and correspondence instructions; source-specific portal-code comparison.
review_scope.not_reviewed: Trial form and detailed evidence-admissibility authorities; no case-specific litigation. Complete division allocation remains county reconciliation.

conflicts.subject: Order formatting
statements: Judge profile expressly says not to use e-Portal formatting codes and requires email submission
Linked shared circuit guide reviewed with Lambert says proposed orders must include DJMCA codes
conflicts.disposition: Preserve judge-specific and shared statements without resolving controlling authority. No shared template requirement imported into judge checklist.

conflicts.subject: Office versus evidence delivery address
conflicts.disposition: Both source-labeled addresses retained for their stated purposes; not treated as interchangeable.

gaps: Full division assignment not stated on profile; reconcile county assignment source.
No separate personal judge email or distinct assistant-only telephone established.

citations.locator: Profile contact/address, scheduling, submissions and communication sections

citations.quote: Proposed Orders MUST be submitted in Microsoft Word .docx format.
citations.locator: Reused two-page shared proposed-order guide acquired during Lambert review; contrast with judge-specific no-code instruction, no new retrieval
